title: Insurance and medical claim documents (India)
description: PII taxonomy for health-insurance claim bundles. Redacts the patient's and claim filer's identity, signatures and every provider-identity carrier; keeps clinical content including test names, values, units and reference ranges.
owner_rules: Redact patient / claim-filer personal identifying details: name, IDs, address, faces
Redact bank information unique to a person; keep common banking infrastructure
Redact signatures, hospital name and the name of the lab that conducted tests
KEEP medical tests and their values
Clinicians pseudonymised to a stable token (owner decision 2026-09-23)
Provider identity redacted across ALL carriers (owner decision 2026-09-23)
bank_line:
THE TEST, applied per value — not a list to memorise: a banking value DIES if it is drawn from a space indexed per CUSTOMER or per ACCOUNT; it SURVIVES if it is drawn from a space indexed per BRANCH or per INSTITUTION. Operationally: could this exact string be printed identically on the statements of thousands of other customers of the same branch? If yes it is common and it stays. If it indexes one account holder, it is 'unique to the person' in the owner's words and it dies.

DIES (account- and customer-space):
- account no; b) account number — the core account-space key. REDACT, never MASK_PARTIAL: the last four digits are a live verification challenge at Indian banks.
- cust id — the bank's customer index, identical in kind to an MRN.
- d) cheque / dd payable details and the cheque/reference no. column — instrument numbers come from one person's cheque book, and the payable-to string is a person's name.
- The E13B MICR strip printed on a cancelled cheque image — it encodes the account number; caught by T12 as symbology, not by OCR.
- a/c open date and od limit — both are per-account facts; the open date also takes the bundle offset as a date.
- The account-holder name and address block in a statement or passbook header — a person's name and address that happen to sit on bank stationery (T01/T15).
- Card numbers anywhere (Luhn).
- Statement row VALUES: withdrawal, deposit, running/closing balance, narration/particulars text, per-row dates (T32, MASK_PARTIAL — the column, header and row alignment survive). A running balance series is a function of one account's entire history, so it is account-space by definition; an Indian narration routinely embeds a UPI VPA (name-or-phone@psp), a counterparty name and a phone number.
- UPI/VPA handles and 10-digit mobile numbers wherever they appear, including on a payment receipt or a bill footer's 'paid via UPI' line — value-level, not column-scoped (T14).

SURVIVES (branch- and institution-space):
- c) bank name and branch; account branch; branch code; rtgs/neft ifsc / micr / branch code; e) ifsc code; micr (branch code as printed on the stationery) — an IFSC addresses a branch shared by hundreds of thousands of customers and carries zero person-specific entropy.
- account type (savings/current); account status.
- The bank's logo, tagline, letterhead and its own GSTIN.
- Statement period label, column headers, row count and table geometry.

ENFORCEMENT AND THE ONE TRAP: the IFSC/MICR structural validators are used in REVERSE here — as a protective veto so a generic 'bank-looking alphanumeric' detector cannot eat a kept value. That veto MUST be gated on the printed label and its position inside the branch-details block. A purely structural veto is a leak: many Indian account numbers are 9 digits or contain a 9-digit run, would match the branch-MICR validator, and would be affirmatively PROTECTED from redaction by the very rule meant to preserve common infrastructure. Outside the branch block, no shape-based protection applies.
provider_deid_spec:
Rule (3) says the hospital name and the lab name die. In this corpus provider identity is not a field: it is roughly a dozen co-occurring carriers on nearly every one of 2,043 pages, in colour, as pixels. A rule that removes only the printed name is theatre. Two geometric regimes, and they must not be confused — this is where the 74% incident came from:
  - GEOMETRY-BOUND rules (logo, seal, stamp, letterhead/footer band fill) fire ONLY in the top 0-18% band, the bottom 88-100% band, or on a detected mark. Inside a band, content still routes by its own label: a patient sticker in the header band is T13, not a provider block.
  - STRING-BOUND rules (gazetteer-matched provider name, legal entity, domain, GSTIN/CIN) fire PAGE-WIDE and unbounded, because a provider word occurs between 18% and 85% of page height on 156 of 432 text-layer pages in 19 of 24 bundles ('name of hospital where admitted' is a mid-page claim-form field).
The gazetteer is built ONCE AT CORPUS LEVEL — names, legal suffixes, trade names, domains, GSTIN and CIN strings harvested from all text-layer pages and the highest-dpi instance of each provider — never bootstrapped per bundle, because four bundles (patient-1..4, 459 pages) have zero text-layer pages and would learn nothing.

WHAT DIES, item by item, with mechanism and box:
1. Letterhead wordmark set as type -> PSEUDONYMIZE to [HOSPITAL_1]/[LAB_1] in the vacated glyph box. value_propagated against the corpus gazetteer, OCR-tolerant match (consistency rule 2). Box = matched token run only.
2. Logo raster and colour wordmark -> REDACT. objective_visual: native image XObject on born-digital pages; on the 79% image-only pages, per-provider template matched by colour histogram + normalised cross-correlation, restricted to the header band. Box = matched component dilated 10%. Precondition: greyscale/bitonal page -> template path only, never chroma.
3. Footer legal name, footer branch address, footer mob/email/web, footer branch GST -> REDACT as one clipped block. label_anchored on the bottom band, firing only when the band carries >=2 of {legal suffix (Ltd/Pvt/Hospital/Clinic/Labs/Diagnostics), validated GSTIN/CIN, 'www.', '@', 6-digit PIN, 'Regd/Branch'}; box clipped to the contiguous text rows carrying those tokens, never expanded to the band, never to the page.
4. Letterhead phone, mobile, website, email and bare domain -> REDACT. Same gated band rule. The brand token inside the domain also feeds the gazetteer so 'riverbendcare' dies mid-page as a string.
5. Rubber-stamp impressions and NABH/NABL seals -> REDACT. objective_visual: closed elliptical/circular/rounded-rect contours in a non-black ink hue, no OCR required; on greyscale scans, contour + template fallback, because the chroma path silently returns zero regions there.
6. Provider GSTIN, branch GST, CIN, NABH/NABL number, drug licence, clinical-establishment registration -> REDACT. checksum: GSTIN 15-char and CIN 21-char structural validators, page-wide.
7. Mid-page provider name fields -> PSEUDONYMIZE. label_anchored on 'name of hospital where admitted', 'facility', 'location', 'sample processed at', 'referred to'. Unbounded by zone.
8. Institution string burned into imaging/CTG raster banners -> REDACT with the rest of the banner (T23). Never the imaged sector.
9. Provider template/form fingerprint -> MASK_PARTIAL: alphabetic run matching a gazetteer entity or acronym dies, numeric and revision portion survives.
10. Provider name and brand in the PDF container (Title, Producer, filename) -> REDACT (T39).

WHAT SURVIVES, deliberately:
- The token [HOSPITAL_1]/[LAB_1] itself, stable across the bundle, so 'one provider across these 90 pages' and 'the lab is not the hospital' remain answerable.
- Facility STATE (city is a per-bundle escalation, see residual risks). Department, ward, bed, theatre, floor and all intra-hospital location labels.
- Letterhead band geometry, rule lines, typography, table structure, column headers, page furniture — the genre classifier's replacement feature set.
- The insurer and TPA entirely (T30), including their logo, addresses and standard form designations.
- The bank's name, branch, IFSC, logo and letterhead (T33) — a bank is not a treating provider.
- Every clinical mark on the page, protected by the T37 veto: a provider box that overlaps a detected clinical table or an imaged sector is rejected and logged, not applied.

WHAT BREAKS, stated rather than hidden:
- Genre classification currently keys on the letterhead. After this pass it must be retrained on band geometry, logo footprint (not content), typography, form-code numerics and table structure. The drop must be MEASURED pre- and post-pass before ship, not asserted.
- Referral chains ('sample processed at X for hospital Y') survive only as token-to-token relations, and only within a bundle.
- Bill GST arithmetic can no longer be validated against a real registration number.
- Referral slips and letterhead-only pages become nearly empty; they should be flagged low-content rather than silently shipped.
- Any page whose only provider carrier is a sub-100-dpi stamp may retain a humanly-legible impression that no mechanism localised. That is a known miss, not a solved case.
consistency_rules: CARRIER LEDGER, per value, not per page. The same MRN appears 40+ times per bundle in at least six carrier classes: printed text, pen ink, sticker, 1D barcode, burned-in imaging banner, and PDF container metadata. Once a value is learned, the bundle does not pass QA until every carrier class is accounted for on every page — a text hit, an ink region, a sticker rectangle, a symbol redaction, a banner box, or an explicit 'carrier absent' assertion. A page-level 'no detections' result is a failure of the ledger, not a clean page.

MATCHING MUST BE OCR-TOLERANT, AND TODAY IT IS NOT. value_propagated as built normalises whitespace and case and then does a literal substring test. At 109 dpi that matches the clean instance and misses every degraded one, so the taxonomy's central promise silently fails. Before ship: normalised edit distance <= 0.2 over token runs, honorific stripped, plus a confusable map (0/O, 1/l/I, 5/S, 8/B, 2/Z) applied before comparison. Report matcher recall per bundle; an unfixed matcher makes every PSEUDONYMIZE row a partial redaction.

GAZETTEERS ARE BUILT AT CORPUS LEVEL, PROPAGATION IS APPLIED AT BUNDLE LEVEL. Provider names, legal entities, domains, GSTIN/CIN and clinician names are harvested once across all 432 text-layer pages and the highest-dpi instance of each mark; four bundles (patient-1..4, 459 pages) have zero text-layer pages and can learn nothing from themselves. Person values are learned and propagated strictly within a bundle. Seeding is source-agnostic: any page clearing an OCR-confidence threshold may seed, with N-page agreement required for low-confidence seeds.

TOKENS ARE DETERMINISTIC, NOT SEQUENTIAL. A token is a keyed hash of (normalised value, role), so the same value produces the same token on every page, in every rendering and on every re-run, and a re-run after a pipeline change does not renumber the corpus. Role disambiguation is arithmetic (if the insured string matches the patient string, collapse to [PATIENT_1]); no model decides who is who.

ONE DATE OFFSET PER BUNDLE, APPLIED TO EVERY PARSED CALENDAR DATE IN EVERY GENRE — admission, discharge, bill, ledger, generation stamp, account-open, LMP, EDD, implant expiry. Any value that parses as a full calendar date takes the offset even when it sits inside a KEEP category; that is the single exception where a date rule beats the clinical KEEP presumption. Exempting one date class (LMP was exempted in two drafts, and appears on 52 pages across 11 bundles) lets an adversary subtract and recover the offset, un-shifting the entire bundle.

SEMANTIC COLUMNS ARE RESOLVED ONCE PER TABLE, THEN APPLIED WHOLE-COLUMN. The same semantic column ('amount', 'balance', 'test value') appears under different headers and positions across bill_breakup, hospital_bill_summary and bank_document layouts. Resolve header string -> canonical column, fall back to position, then apply the action to the whole column x-range for every row. Per-cell decisions at 109 dpi produce 11-of-13 rows treated one way and 2 another, which is the inconsistency the owner reported.

DETECTOR SILENCE IS DETECTOR FAILURE. Every genre gate may only WIDEN redaction, never narrow it; a misclassified page is over-redacted, not leaked. Every mechanism with a physical precondition declares it: a page with fewer than two chroma levels marks handwriting_ink and stamp-chroma rules NOT-APPLICABLE and routes to fail-closed label_anchored box redaction, instead of returning zero regions that read as 'nothing here'.

PROVIDER GEOMETRY IS ZONE-BOUND, PROVIDER STRINGS ARE NOT. Logo, seal, stamp and band-fill rules fire only in the header/footer bands; gazetteer string matches fire page-wide. Inside a band, content still routes by its own label — a patient sticker in the top-right header band is T13, a bank letterhead is T33, a TPA letterhead is T30. Band membership never assigns an action by itself.

ACTION VOCABULARY MUST EXIST IN CODE. Eleven rows are PSEUDONYMIZE, GENERALIZE or MASK_PARTIAL, while the built redactor has exactly one path (black-fill annotation) and no token store. Until a token store and an overlay-write path exist, every such row silently degrades to REDACT and the taxonomy's utility argument is false. Ship-blocking.

PER-RUN METRICS, REPORTED NOT ASSERTED: pages fully redacted; mean redacted area per page per genre; count and share of regions decided by model_judged (T05 only); carrier-ledger completeness per learned value; matcher recall; genre-classifier accuracy measured before and after the provider pass. Over-redaction must stay visible, because destroying documents — not leaking — is this pipeline's observed failure mode.
residual_risks: Exact monetary amounts are kept (T34). An approved amount, net amount and patient-payable tuple at paisa resolution is effectively unique in any insurer or TPA claims table, and the same figures exist in the insurer's record, the hospital's ledger and the claimant's bank statement. A single equality join re-identifies the bundle to anyone holding one of those tables. This is not fixable inside the taxonomy without destroying the reason the corpus exists.

The surviving quasi-identifier set still supports a small-cohort attack: city, PIN region (3 digits), sex, 5-year age band, relationship, hospital days, department, ward/bed/theatre numbering and the full clinical narrative. On the maternity and paediatric bundles this is women of childbearing age in one metro at one (tokenised but structurally distinctive) facility — a cohort in the tens, not the thousands.

Dates are shifted, not destroyed, by one per-bundle offset. If the keyed offset leaks, or if any un-shifted true date survives anywhere in a bundle — a handwritten date in a clinical note, a date inside an unreadable stamp, a date in an image the banner rule missed — the whole bundle un-shifts in one subtraction.

Clinical content is untouched by instruction, and some of it is directly identifying in substance: a rare diagnosis or rare procedure, a named congenital syndrome, self-inflicted injury cause, MLC/police flags, and maternity delivery context. Rule (4) is honoured; the disclosure exposure is real and is not mitigated anywhere in this taxonomy.

Facility identity survives structurally even after every provider carrier dies: band geometry, logo footprint, typography, form-code numerics, ward/bed/theatre numbering scheme and table layout are a fingerprint strong enough to cluster bundles by provider, and the provider set across 24 bundles is small and closed.

Handwriting on greyscale, bitonal or black-ballpoint pages has no chromatic signal. The fail-closed label_anchored fallback covers labelled fields only; a patient name written in pen into the middle of a progress-note body on such a page is, in the general case, not detected by any deterministic mechanism.

Sub-100-dpi pages (42% of the corpus) degrade every text mechanism at once: QR and barcode decode fails well above 100 dpi (symbols are redacted on detection, but an undetected symbol is not), checksum validation depends on OCR that may not produce candidates, and the fallback's whole-page action is withheld on clinical genres to protect rule (4) — so a low-dpi clinical page with a missed identifier leaks.

Insurer and TPA identity is kept in full (T30). Combined with kept claim amounts and a shifted-but-interval-preserving date sequence, a party holding the TPA's own records can re-identify bundles; this is an accepted trade for genre signal, not an argument that the risk is small.

One category (T05, unlabelled names in prose) is decided by a vision model and will vary page to page and run to run. Its residual leak rate is non-zero, is not estimable in advance, and must be measured and reported per run rather than assumed away.

Tokens are per bundle, so a person or provider appearing in several bundles receives unrelated tokens — which blocks cross-bundle linkage by the adversary but also means the corpus cannot detect that it contains the same patient twice, so duplicate exposure is invisible.

categories.name: PATIENT_NAME
categories.definition: IN: the hospitalized person's name as the value of any name-bearing label on a form, bill, report header, sticker-free page body or salutation, including honorific-attached and 'Baby of <mother>' forms (which also mint the mother's token). OUT: clinicians (T29), insured/nominee/witness (T02, T03), provider organisation names (T24).
categories.corpus_examples: patient name; name; a) name (insured person hospitalized); patient sticker - name (routed to T13)
categories.note: All three lenses agreed; token [PATIENT_1] stamped in the vacated box keeps bill rows, discharge summaries and lab headers linkable, and the printed glyphs are destroyed so this is a redaction plus a label, not a softening of rule (1). Cost: a reviewer can still count how many distinct people a bundle names.

categories.name: RELATED_PARTY_NAME
categories.definition: IN: names of the non-patient natural persons the claim binds — primary insured/proposer, policy holder, primary member, the person a cheque or DD is payable to, and the parent/guardian on a paediatric or maternity file. Distinct token per role; collapse to [PATIENT_1] when the string fuzzy-matches the patient. OUT: nominee/witness/attendant (T03).
categories.corpus_examples: d) name (primary insured); primary member; policy holder; d) cheque / dd payable details
categories.note: The owner named the claim filer explicitly; separate tokens ([INSURED_1], [MEMBER_1]) because whether patient and filer are the same person is itself analysable and would be lost under one token.

categories.name: THIRD_PARTY_PERSON_NAME
categories.definition: IN: nominees, witnesses, accompanying attendants, next-of-kin and any named non-clinical third party on consent forms, claim declarations and KYC pages, plus their contact details and relationship-by-name. OUT: the insured and filer (T02); clinicians (T29).
categories.corpus_examples: nomination; consent_form (x4) attendant/witness blocks; kyc_form_individual related-person fields
categories.note: Extension: a witness on a consent form is neither patient nor filer, but they never consented to the corpus and the token costs nothing analytically; unlabelled third parties fall to T22/T05 and will be less consistent.

categories.name: NAME_IN_FREE_TEXT
categories.definition: IN: any occurrence of a name already learned elsewhere in the bundle (T01, T02, T03, T29) appearing mid-sentence in prose — progress notes, discharge summaries, consent bodies, operation notes, 'amount in words' payee phrases, imaging indications. Replaced with the same token as the labelled occurrence.
categories.corpus_examples: discharge_summary (x9) and doctor_progress_notes (x3) bodies; consent_form body text; amount in words
categories.note: Field-level action alone leaks: the name is read cleanly once on the claim form and then reappears unlabelled in prose; this row is only as good as the fuzzy matcher required by consistency rule 2, which the current exact-substring implementation does not provide.

categories.name: UNSEEN_NAME_IN_PROSE
categories.definition: IN: a personal or organisational name in running prose that matches no bundle-learned value and has no printed label — 'discussed with Dr Menon at Apollo', a relative named only in a nursing note. Any hit is fed back into T04's value set and struck deterministically on all remaining pages.
categories.corpus_examples: patient complaints; chief complaints; ophthalmic history; systemic history; condition of the patient during discharge
categories.note: This is the ONLY model_judged row and therefore the only page-to-page-variable one — the exact behaviour the owner complained about; it is contained by running last, only on regions no deterministic row claimed, and by converting every hit into a deterministic bundle-wide strike.

categories.name: POLICY_MEMBERSHIP_ID
categories.definition: IN: every identifier indexing this person inside an insurer, TPA, employer scheme or government scheme database — policy number, member ID, MA-ID, company/TPA ID, enrolment number, certificate serial. Stable per-role token. OUT: hospital-issued keys (T07), government ID numbers (T08), bank identifiers (T31).
categories.corpus_examples: a) policy no; c) company/ tpa id no; member id; enrolment no; ma-id; b) sl. no/certificate no
categories.note: Highest-yield linking keys in the corpus — one policy number joins every bundle of a family across years — and the label region is redacted even when the handwritten value itself is unreadable at 109 dpi.

categories.name: PROVIDER_ASSIGNED_PATIENT_ID
categories.definition: IN: the provider's own person and episode keys — MRN, MR no, MPI, MPID, UHID, patient ID, IP number — wherever printed outside a sticker. OUT: the same numbers inside a sticker (T13), inside a barcode (T12) or burned into an imaging banner (T23), each of which has its own carrier rule.
categories.corpus_examples: patient id; mrn no; mpi#; mr no; mpid; ip#
categories.note: This is the value that recurs 40+ times per bundle in four renderings, so it is the row that consistency rule 1's carrier ledger exists for; propagation from a clean read is what covers the sub-100-dpi ward pages.

categories.name: GOVERNMENT_ID_NUMBER
categories.definition: IN: Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, driving licence, passport, CKYC number and police FIR number naming the person, wherever printed including as a field on a bank or claim form. Never MASK_PARTIAL. OUT: provider registration codes (T27); bank account numbers (T31).
categories.corpus_examples: a) pan; id number; kyc_form_individual (CERSAI Central KYC) fields
categories.note: Checksum (Verhoeff/Luhn/PAN-GSTIN structural) fires on the value's own arithmetic so it survives an unreadable label, with confusable-digit expansion before validation; partial masking is forbidden because PAN's fifth character is the holder's surname initial and the last four of an account number are a live verification challenge.

categories.name: ID_DOCUMENT_PAGE
categories.definition: IN: a page whose subject is a photo-ID or KYC artefact — Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, passport, driving licence, insurance ID card, CERSAI KYC form. The page body is destroyed to a stub that retains only the document-type caption and page number. OUT: a claim form that merely quotes an ID number (T08).
categories.corpus_examples: id_document (x19); insurance_id_card (x2); kyc_form_individual (CERSAI Central KYC)
categories.note: OWNER 2026-09-23: demoted from page-level destruction to KEEP. Firing it on a CKYC form destroyed 107 boxes of PRINTED, EMPTY form scaffolding on one page - labels with no values behind them. A page-level 'destroy the body' action cannot distinguish a filled ID card from a blank form, so the identity on an ID page is now removed by the value-level rows that can: T08 (checksum-verified government numbers), T10 (faces), T12 (QR and barcode), T01/T02 (names), T15 (address). Residual: an identity value on an image-only ID page that no value-level row localises now survives.

categories.name: FACE_PHOTOGRAPH
categories.definition: IN: every human face image — ID and KYC portraits, insurance-card photos, faces in wound or clinical photographs, a portrait recovered from a decoded Aadhaar QR — plus the whole portrait box on the identity genres whether or not a face is detected inside it. OUT: clinical imagery (ultrasound, fundus, radiographs, CTG), which is T37.
categories.corpus_examples: id_document photo regions; insurance_id_card (x2); native image XObjects embedded in claim_form_partA
categories.note: Vision face rectangles UNION native image XObjects UNION the fixed photo-box geometry of the identity genres — the union is the fail-closed part, because face detection is unreliable on a low-dpi photocopy and that is exactly where ID cards live.

categories.name: SIGNATURE_AND_THUMBPRINT
categories.definition: IN: every handwritten signature, initial, monogram and inked thumb impression by anyone — patient, relative, witness, doctor, nurse, authorised signatory, bank verifier — including the specimen signature on a cancelled cheque and initials in medication and nursing cells. OUT: handwritten clinical values (T37) and handwritten identity values (T22).
categories.corpus_examples: consent_form (x4); claim_form_partA (x12) declaration blocks; surgical_safety_checklist (x2); d) cheque / dd payable details
categories.note: label_anchored on the enumerable printed captions ('Signature', 'Sign', 'Thumb impression', 'Authorised', 'Witness') is the primary and fires unconditionally, with handwriting_ink only trimming the box inside it — because chromatic segmentation returns nothing on a greyscale scan or a black-ballpoint signature and would otherwise fail silently.

categories.name: MACHINE_READABLE_CODE
categories.definition: IN: every 1D barcode, QR, DataMatrix and PDF417 on any page, and the E13B MICR strip on a cheque image, redacted on DETECTION whether or not the payload decodes. OUT: printed human-readable serials, which route to their own rows.
categories.corpus_examples: barcode no; qr code (bottom right); patient sticker - barcode
categories.note: Fail-closed by construction: an undecodable symbol is precisely the case where we cannot prove it harmless, and at 42% of pages below 100 dpi against a ~300 dpi floor for dense QR decode, undecodable is the normal case; a redacted MRN beside an intact barcode of the same MRN is a silent leak.

categories.name: PATIENT_STICKER_BLOCK
categories.definition: IN: the pre-printed adhesive patient label as ONE rectangle — name, MPI, IP number, age/sex, date of admission, attending physician and barcode die together, including any constituent that would otherwise be KEEP. OUT: the underlying form's own fields outside the sticker rectangle.
categories.corpus_examples: patient sticker - name; patient sticker - mpi; ip# (patient sticker); patient sticker - age/gender; patient sticker - doa; patient sticker - physician; patient sticker - barcode
categories.note: Found geometrically (barcode anchor plus surrounding high-contrast print block), not as seven OCR reads — seven per-field reads on a scan where two labels are illegible is exactly where the observed inconsistency came from; the sticker sits in the header band and must route here, not to the provider band rule.

categories.name: PERSONAL_CONTACT_CHANNEL
categories.definition: IN: mobile and landline numbers, email addresses and UPI/VPA handles belonging to the patient, insured, nominee or attendant, anywhere on the page — as a labelled field value, in prose, or in a receipt's 'paid via UPI' line. OUT, as a hard veto: every phone, email, URL and domain inside the provider letterhead/footer bands (T26), the insurer/TPA block (T30) and the bank's own stationery (T33).
categories.corpus_examples: phone no; email id; UPI VPA strings on payment_receipt; footer: mob/email/web (VETOED — provider)
categories.note: Contested because the lenses split between a label-only rule (misses VPAs and prose numbers) and a page-wide regex (this is what produced the 74%-of-a-page box); the synthesis runs label_anchored plus a structural validator (10-digit starting 6-9, RFC email, local@known-PSP) page-wide, gated by an explicit PROTECTED list of provider/payer/bank strings so a provider footer email can never be classified as personal PII.

categories.name: PERSONAL_POSTAL_ADDRESS
categories.definition: IN: the house/flat number, building, street, locality and landmark lines of the residential address of the patient, insured or nominee, taken as the full multi-line value block from the 'Address' label to the next printed label or rule line. OUT: pin/city/state (T16); any hospital, bank-branch, insurer or employer address (T26, T33, T30).
categories.corpus_examples: address; g) address (if different from above); e) address (primary insured)
categories.note: Destroyed rather than tokenised because the block is multi-line and usually handwritten, so there is no reliable string to tokenise; taking the whole labelled region means an unreadable handwritten address still dies.

categories.name: PATIENT_GEO_COARSE
categories.definition: IN: the pin code, city and state of the person's residence. PIN is truncated to its first three digits (postal region); city and state survive verbatim. OUT: street-level components (T15); a city or state printed as part of a hospital, bank or insurer address (T26, T33, T30).
categories.corpus_examples: pin code; city; state
categories.note: Extension, and the one place this taxonomy deliberately does not destroy: the owner said 'address', not 'geography'; two lenses kept a 4-digit PIN prefix and an adversary showed 6000xx is a single Chennai cluster, so the minimal fix is three digits — the residual city+region+cohort risk is stated in residual_risks rather than argued away.

categories.name: DATE_OF_BIRTH
categories.definition: IN: the stated date of birth of the patient, insured or nominee — coarsened to year only. EXCEPTION: for a patient under two years, DOB takes the bundle date offset instead of coarsening, so age-in-days arithmetic survives for neonatal and paediatric files. OUT: every other date (T21).
categories.corpus_examples: dob; d) date of birth; neonate DOB on maternity bundles
categories.note: Owner override 2026-09-23: dates kept exact. The facility+date join this would have blocked is broken on the provider side instead. (was GENERALIZE in the synthesis.)

categories.name: AGE_SEX_RELATIONSHIP
categories.definition: IN: age (banded to 5 years for adults; exact in months/days under 2; 90+ collapsed to a single band), sex/gender (KEPT verbatim), relationship to the primary insured and policy-holder role marker (KEPT verbatim). OUT: DOB (T17); gestational age, age-at-onset and paediatric dosing weights, which are clinical (T37).
categories.corpus_examples: age; age/sex; age/gender; gender; b) gender: male/female; c) age: years/months; relation; e) relationship to primary insured
categories.note: Sex and relationship are named as explicit KEEPs so no later reader sweeps them in as quasi-identifiers — they are low-entropy and structurally required to read a family-floater claim; age banding is arithmetic, not judgement.

categories.name: OCCUPATION_AND_EMPLOYER
categories.definition: IN: free-text occupation and employer detail on group-policy claim forms and the sponsoring company name. Occupation maps to a broad ISCO-style class; any string outside the closed vocabulary is REDACTED rather than passed through. Employer name becomes [EMPLOYER_1]. OUT: the employee code (T20); the hospital as an employer of clinicians (T24).
categories.corpus_examples: f) occupation; c) if yes, company name
categories.note: Extension and the weakest-justified row here: 'Senior pilot, Indigo, Chennai' is identifying and 'Transport' is not, but group-policy analytics by employer is destroyed — if the owner wants employer-level analysis, KEEP the company name and accept a corporate-directory join risk.

categories.name: EMPLOYEE_CODE
categories.definition: IN: the staff or employee number issued to the insured by their employer. OUT: the employer's name (T19); the insurer's member ID (T06).
categories.corpus_examples: employee code
categories.note: Extension in name only — an employee code indexes exactly one person inside a known company, which is squarely rule (1)'s 'IDs'; REDACT not tokenise, because nothing downstream needs to link two occurrences of it.

categories.name: EPISODE_AND_CLINICAL_DATE
categories.definition: IN: EVERY value in the bundle that parses as a full calendar date, in every genre and every category — admission, discharge, injury/onset, visit, exam, sample collection, report, bill, generation, validity, account-open, transaction and value dates, AND clinical calendar anchors including LMP and EDD. One keyed per-bundle offset is applied to all of them. Times of day, durations, hospital days and gestational age in weeks are untouched. OUT: DOB (T17).
categories.corpus_examples: e) date of admission; g) date of discharge; admitted on; discharged on; visit date; exam date; bill date; generated on; valid upto; lmp date; a/c open date; transaction date column; value date column
categories.note: Owner override 2026-09-23: dates kept exact, so intervals, waiting periods and turnaround times survive for adjudication. (was GENERALIZE in the synthesis.)

categories.name: HANDWRITTEN_IDENTITY_INK
categories.definition: IN: pen ink falling inside an identity zone — a region anchored by a name, UHID, address, phone, policy, DOB or signature label, the top and footer bands, and any form field whose printed label is an identity label. OUT, and this is the point of the row: pen ink in clinical zones — vitals cells, dosing columns, progress-note bodies, anaesthesia charts — which is KEPT under rule (4).
categories.corpus_examples: claim_form_partA (x12) and vitals_chart (x8) handwritten entries; nursing_admission_assessment (x2); consent_form blanks
categories.note: Decides by WHERE the ink is, never by reading it, because at 109 dpi no OCR will read handwriting; the fail-closed clause is mandatory — on a greyscale or bitonal page the chromatic path is NOT-APPLICABLE and the identity-labelled value box is redacted unconditionally by label_anchored, since otherwise the mechanism reports 'no ink' on exactly the worst pages.

categories.name: IMAGE_BURNED_IN_BANNER
categories.definition: IN: the non-image header and footer text rows rendered into the pixels of ultrasound, CTG, fundus and radiology frames — patient name, ID, study date/time, operator initials AND the institution string in the same banner. OUT, emphatically: the imaged sector itself and every measurement, calliper, waveform and annotation inside it.
categories.corpus_examples: imaging_report (x20); ctg_fetal_monitoring_strip; ophthalmic_examination_report frames
categories.note: imaging_report is the largest catalogued genre and its identity lives in the raster, not in a field, so a text-field pipeline leaves every one of these pages fully identified; the banner is found as the text rows above/below the image sector, and the sector is protected by the T37 veto so a mis-sized box cannot eat the study.

categories.name: PROVIDER_NAME_TEXT
categories.definition: IN: every textual rendering of the treating hospital, clinic, diagnostic centre or laboratory name — letterhead wordmark set as type, footer legal name, the name inside a rubber stamp, the 'facility' field, 'name of hospital where admitted', 'sample processed at', referral lines, and the email domain's brand token. OUT: the insurer and TPA (T30); the bank (T33).
categories.corpus_examples: a) name of hospital where admitted; facility; footer: hospital legal name; hospital rubber stamp (childrens clinic india ltd.); location
categories.note: [HOSPITAL_1]/[LAB_1] rather than a black box keeps 'same provider across these 90 pages' and 'the lab is not the hospital' answerable, which is most of what the genre classifier and the annotator actually used the letterhead for; the string set comes from a CORPUS-level gazetteer, because four bundles have zero text-layer pages to learn from.

categories.name: PROVIDER_VISUAL_MARK
categories.definition: IN: the hospital/lab logo raster and colour wordmark, the NABH/NABL/ISO accreditation seal, departmental crests, and inked rubber-stamp impressions carrying a facility name or registration line. OUT: the bank's logo and tagline (T33); the insurer/TPA logo (T30); clinical images (T37).
categories.corpus_examples: hospital logo (riverbend); nabh accreditation seal; hospital rubber stamp (childrens clinic india ltd.)
categories.note: A logo is identity in pixels and survives at 96 dpi where the type does not, so redacting the name and leaving the mark is theatre; native image XObjects on born-digital pages, and on scans a per-provider template matched by colour histogram plus normalised cross-correlation inside the band — with a colour-space precondition, since a stamp rule keyed to violet ink silently returns nothing on a greyscale scan.

categories.name: PROVIDER_CONTACT_BLOCK
categories.definition: IN: the treating provider's postal and branch address, landline, mobile, website and email including the bare domain, in the letterhead band (top 0-18%) or the footer band (bottom 88-100%). The band fires only when it carries >=2 of {legal suffix, validated GSTIN/CIN, 'www.', '@', 6-digit PIN, 'Regd/Branch'}, and the box is clipped to the contiguous text rows carrying those tokens. OUT: the patient's own contact details (T14); the bank's and insurer's stationery (T33, T30).
categories.corpus_examples: phone (letterhead); website (letterhead); email; hospital postal address (letterhead); footer: branch address; footer: mob/email/web
categories.note: These resolve to the hospital in one web lookup, so keeping them nullifies rule (3); the band gate plus row clipping is the direct fix for the 74% incident, where a free page-wide email regex classified info@riverbendcare.com as personal PII and licensed an aggressive personal-PII box.

categories.name: PROVIDER_REGISTRATION_CODE
categories.definition: IN: the treating provider's GSTIN and branch GST number, CIN, NABH/NABL accreditation number, drug licence and clinical-establishment registration number, wherever they appear. OUT: a person's PAN (T08); the insurer's or TPA's own GSTIN/CIN on their stationery (T30); a bank's GSTIN (T33).
categories.corpus_examples: cin; gstn#; footer: gst no. (branch)
categories.note: Marked EXTENSION because the owner named the hospital's NAME — but a GSTIN returns the registered legal name and principal place of business from a free public registry in one query, so it is the name in numeric form; cost, stated plainly: GST-line arithmetic on bills is no longer verifiable against a real registration.

categories.name: PROVIDER_FORM_FINGERPRINT
categories.definition: IN: the provider's pre-printed template identifier (e.g. a corner 'CN/OPD/F-023 Rev.2') and 'Form No' lines unique to that provider's stationery — the alphabetic run matching a gazetteer provider name or acronym is destroyed, the numeric and revision portion survives. OUT: regulator-standard form designations published by the insurer or IRDAI (T30, T38).
categories.corpus_examples: form version code; b) sl. no/certificate no (form-designation portion)
categories.note: Extension: a template code is a stable cross-bundle fingerprint that re-identifies the provider after name and logo are gone, but destroying it whole would remove a genre cue for zero extra privacy — partial masking resolves the contradiction the drafts had between 'keep form codes' and 'kill organisational carriers'.

categories.name: CLINICIAN_IDENTITY
categories.definition: IN: names and medical-registration numbers of doctors, surgeons, anaesthetists, referring physicians, radiologists, pathologists and named nursing staff, in fields, consultant strips and report sign-offs. OUT: their specialty, department, role and qualifications, which survive verbatim; their signature (T11).
categories.corpus_examples: surgeon; doctor; referred by; patient sticker - physician; report sign-off lines in doctor_progress_notes
categories.note: Extension — the owner scoped patient and filer — but all three lenses reached it independently because rule (3) is void without it: 'Dr <rare surname>, Consultant Obstetrician' plus a public Indian medical register names the hospital in one lookup.

categories.name: INSURER_TPA_IDENTITY
categories.definition: IN: the insurer's and third-party administrator's name, logo, registered and corporate addresses, helpline, licence number and their published standard form designations. OUT: the person-bound policy and member IDs printed on their forms (T06); the treating provider (T24-T28).
categories.corpus_examples: medi assist insurance tpa private limited; tpa registered address; tpa corporate address; insurance_id_card issuer marks
categories.note: An explicit KEEP, checked BEFORE the provider band rule fires so a TPA letterhead is never mistaken for a treating-provider letterhead; the TPA is the claim's recipient, not a treating party, appears across most bundles and carries near-zero discriminating power — and it is most of the surviving genre signal.

categories.name: PERSON_BANK_INSTRUMENT
categories.definition: IN: banking values drawn from a space indexed per customer or per account — account number, customer ID, cheque and DD numbers and payable-to details, the cheque's E13B MICR line, card numbers, the account-holder name/address block on a statement or passbook header, account-opening date, sanctioned OD limit. OUT: everything branch- or institution-scoped (T33).
categories.corpus_examples: account no; b) account number; cust id; d) cheque / dd payable details; a/c open date; od limit
categories.note: label_anchored is the primary because no checksum exists for Indian account numbers, with Luhn/structural validators only used to trim the box; never MASK_PARTIAL, since the last four digits of an account number are a standard live verification challenge.

categories.name: BANK_LEDGER_ROW_VALUES
categories.definition: IN: the cell values of a personal statement or passbook — narration/particulars text, cheque/reference number column, withdrawal, deposit and running/closing balance figures, per-row dates. Column headers, row count, table geometry and the statement period label survive; the values inside them do not. OUT: hospital bill line items and claim amounts (T34).
categories.corpus_examples: withdrawal amt. column; deposit amt. column; closing balance column; cheque/reference no. column; transaction date column; value date column
categories.note: Extension over a literal reading of rule (2), justified by the owner's own test: a running balance series is a function of one account's entire history and an Indian narration string routinely embeds a UPI VPA, a counterparty name and a phone number — so it is person-unique; masked whole-column at the header x-range, which is far more consistent at 109 dpi than per-cell detection.

categories.name: COMMON_BANK_INFRASTRUCTURE
categories.definition: IN, untouched: bank name, branch name and address, branch code, IFSC, the branch MICR code, RTGS/NEFT routing codes, account type, account status, the bank's logo, tagline and letterhead. OUT: anything account- or customer-scoped (T31, T32).
categories.corpus_examples: c) bank name and branch; e) ifsc code; branch code; account branch; rtgs/neft ifsc / micr / branch code; micr; account type; account status; hdfc bank logo + tagline
categories.note: Rule (2)'s 'leave common things alone' half, enforced as a protective veto so a generic bank-looking-alphanumeric detector cannot eat an IFSC — but the veto is gated on the printed label AND its position inside the branch-details block, because many Indian account numbers are 9 digits and would otherwise be structurally 'protected' as branch MICR codes, which would be a leak created by a KEEP rule.

categories.name: CLAIM_FINANCIAL_AMOUNT
categories.definition: IN, untouched: every rupee figure and quantity produced by the hospital or insurer for this episode — sum insured, bill/net/approved amounts, line items, discounts, advance adjustments, refunds, insurance and patient payable, amounts in words (minus any embedded payee name, which is T04), payment mode, quantity columns. OUT: personal bank ledger values (T32).
categories.corpus_examples: sum insured (rs.); total; bill amount; net amount; approved amount; adv adj to bill; amount received from patient; amount refunded; insurance payable; patient payable; discount(md); line-item amount values
categories.note: Stated as an explicit KEEP so nobody later sweeps amounts in as 'financial PII' — these amounts are why the corpus exists; the attack (an exact approved-amount plus hospital-days tuple is a near-unique equality join against an insurer's claims table) is real, not fixable inside the taxonomy without destroying the analytic payload, and is therefore carried as a residual risk and an owner decision. OWNER 2026-09-23: hospital expenses, totals, bill break-up lines, GST and package-discount rows are the agent's task input and must survive intact.

categories.name: DOCUMENT_SERIAL
categories.definition: IN: numbers indexing this episode's documents in the provider's system — bill number, invoice number, visit number, visit ID/ref number, accession/report reference — replaced with stable per-bundle tokens ([BILL_1], [VISIT_1]). OUT: page numbers, report status and form designations (T38).
categories.corpus_examples: bill no; invoice no; visit no; visit id/ref no
categories.note: Extension: these index a document, not a person — but bill numbers in this corpus routinely embed the MRN and date, and a bill number resolves to the named patient inside the hospital's billing system; tokenising keeps the 13 bill_breakup pages joinable to their summary, which a redaction would break.

categories.name: IMPLANT_DEVICE_IDENTIFIER
categories.definition: IN: lot, batch, serial and UDI strings on implant inventory labels and device stickers, tokenised per bundle; the sterilisation expiry date takes the bundle date offset. OUT: make, model, size, material, quantity and price, which are clinical and commercial content and survive verbatim.
categories.corpus_examples: post_op_instruction_sheet_with_implant_inventory peel-off label set
categories.note: Extension raised by one lens's adversary and accepted: a UDI/serial is a globally unique manufacturer key that distributors trace to a hospital, date and patient, so it is an indirect person key wearing a clinical label — the medical content of the sheet is untouched.

categories.name: CLINICAL_CONTENT
categories.definition: IN, untouchable: test and panel names, results, units, reference ranges, methods, sample types, vitals, diagnoses, procedures, departments, allergies, blood group, anaesthesia and medication records, imaging findings, measurements and the imaged sector itself, gestational and fetal biometry, ophthalmic values, complaints, histories, indications, routes, discharge condition and review advice. OUT: calendar dates inside clinical text (T21); names inside clinical prose (T04, T05).
categories.corpus_examples: test name (cell value); b.p; pulse; temp; diagnosis; sample type; blood group; iop(1); keratometry values; refraction data; estimated fetal weight; indication(s); route
categories.note: Rule (4) promoted from an outcome to an enforced invariant: this row is a veto — any proposed box overlapping a detected clinical table, results region or imaged sector is rejected and logged for review rather than applied, and no detector runs on this content, which is the strongest available consistency guarantee.

categories.name: LAYOUT_AND_ADMIN_METADATA
categories.definition: IN, untouched: page numbers, printed field labels themselves (including the label of every masked field), table rules and column headers, section titles, report status, yes/no legal flags, MLC and police-report flags, intra-hospital location labels (department, ward, bed, theatre, floor), blank-page markers, and insurer-published standard form designations. OUT: anything carrying an organisational name or acronym (T24, T28).
categories.corpus_examples: page no; report status; reported to police yes/no; mlc report & police fir attached; department; blank_scanned_page (x3)
categories.note: Stated explicitly so MASK_PARTIAL rows have a defined 'what survives' and an annotator can see that a field existed and was suppressed rather than never present; label_anchored detection depends on this scaffolding, so destroying it would degrade every other row.

categories.name: DOCUMENT_CONTAINER_METADATA
categories.definition: IN: PDF Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Producer and creation/modification timestamps, XMP packets, bookmarks/TOC entries, annotations, embedded files and attachment names, and the output filename itself — all scrubbed, the file renamed to its bundle token. OUT: page content, which is covered by every other row.
categories.corpus_examples: PDF titles measured to carry patient given names and the provider brand (e.g. '<given-name>_redacted', '<given-name>-riverbend')
categories.note: Extension in form, mechanically compelled by rules (1) and (3): the taxonomy is otherwise page-scoped and the patient's given name and the hospital brand survive in the container in at least four bundles, which defeats both rules with no page-level detector ever firing; the enumerator is the same document-object pass that finds image XObjects, extended to the container dictionary.

categories.name: UNRESOLVED_PAGE_FALLBACK
categories.definition: IN: any page where detection is not trustworthy — OCR under ~40 tokens or below the confidence floor, estimated dpi under 100 with zero label anchors matched, or genre unknown. Non-clinical or identity-dense page: whole page destroyed. CLINICAL genre page: letterhead band, footer band, all pen ink and all detected image objects destroyed, body content left intact. OUT: blank_scanned_page, which is dropped, not blacked out.
categories.corpus_examples: the 42% of pages below 100 dpi generally; id_document and kyc pages whose anchors fail; low-dpi photocopied ward notes
categories.note: Detector silence is treated as detector failure, never as page-is-clean — but the clinical-genre carve-out is mandatory, because a blanket whole-page fallback blacks out imaging films and CTG strips (which legitimately carry almost no text) and that is a direct violation of rule (4); the gate is deterministic page statistics with no model, and pages-fully-redacted must be reported per run so over-redaction stays visible.

lexicon_note: Label vocabulary OWNED BY THIS PACK. It is compiled only when this pack is selected, so adding a claim-form label here cannot change what any other pack sees. That isolation is the point: a label added for the generic pack once matched the tail of a charge-line description ('Amount Received From Patient  0.00') and took the figure beside it.
